Magnet motor with cam
One of the most watched magnet models on the internet.

Four magnets on the rim of the wheel and a fixed magnet at the tip of an arm. A cam on the same axle raises and lowers the arm: it moves the fixed magnet away just as a wheel magnet would reach the “sticky point”, and brings it back once it has passed.

To move the fixed magnet away you have to push it against the force pulling the magnets together, and that push comes from the cam, using the wheel's own energy. What's saved at the sticky point is paid for at the cam, and on top of that the roller, the axle and the hinge rub. In the ledger you'll see that the wheel only spends the energy it had at the start, and stops. Change the cam's lift or angle: no combination gets extra energy out.
